subject: biotechnology
title: Fermentation: Yeast Converts Glucose to Ethanol and Carbon Dioxide

questions.prompt: A student says: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the ethanol and bubbles were not visible before, so they must have been created from nothing

The yeast converts the glucose: as fermentation proceeds the glucose is used up, and that same material reappears as ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas collecting above it - glucose falls by the amount converted.
The glucose did stay the same, and the yeast itself turned into ethanol and gas without using any glucose
The ethanol was already in the flask from the start, hidden in the glucose solution

questions.misconception: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: The alcohol appears from nothing as the mixture ferments, because the glucose in the flask stays the same while ethanol and gas are produced. In fact The yeast converts the glucose: as fermentation proceeds the glucose is used up, and that same material reappears as ethanol in the liquid and carbon dioxide gas collecting above it - glucose falls by the amount converted.

questions.prompt: Which gas is produced by fermentation and collects in the gas space?
questions.explanation: Scenes 2 to 4 work this: carbon dioxide bubbles form in the liquid, rise through it and collect in the gas space above the liquid.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state what happens to the glucose during fermentation.
questions.answer: The yeast takes in the glucose and converts it, so the glucose bar falls steadily until the glucose is almost used up.
questions.explanation: The animation runs the glucose bar down scene by scene as the yeast consumes the glucose: full in s1, falling in s2, low in s3, almost gone in s4.

questions.prompt: Explain why the ethanol bar rises as fermentation proceeds.
questions.answer: The yeast converts the glucose it takes in into ethanol and carbon dioxide, so ethanol builds up in the liquid as the glucose falls - the ethanol is converted glucose, not new material from nothing.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows the ethanol bar rising while the glucose bar falls: the two bars move together because one is converted into the other.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the stages of fermentation in order?

choices.text: Yeast added with glucose full, glucose falls as ethanol and gas appear, glucose low with ethanol and gas grown, glucose used up with products complete
Glucose used up with products complete, glucose low, glucose falls, yeast added with glucose full
Glucose falls as ethanol and gas appear, yeast added with glucose full, glucose used up, glucose low
Yeast added with glucose full, glucose used up at once, glucose low, glucose falls

questions.explanation: The whole animation runs the conversion in that order: s1 yeast added, s2 conversion begins, s3 conversion continues, s4 conversion complete.
